If [MATH: y =7\arcsch(1-x),] then [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}y}{ extrm{d}x}=]

[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}}{ extrm{d}x}(\arcsch x) = -\dfrac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+x^2}}.]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(7arcsch (1 − x)); = 7(d)/(dx)(arcsch (1 − x)); = 7(− (1)/(|1 − x|sqrt(1 + (1 − x)^{2}))) ⋅ (1 − x)^{′}; = 7(− (1)/(|x − 1|sqrt(1 + 1 − 2x + x^{2}))) ⋅ (− 1); = (7)/(|x − 1|sqrt(x^{2} − 2x + 2)).]

If [MATH: y = 5\arsech{2x},] then [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}y}{ extrm{d}x}=]

[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}}{ extrm{d}x}(\arsech x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}.]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get [MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(5arsech 2x); = 5(d)/(dx)(arsech 2x); = 5(− (1)/((2x)sqrt(1 − (2x)^{2}))) ⋅ (2x)^{′}; = − (5)/(2xsqrt(1 − 4x^{2})) ⋅ 2; = − (5)/(xsqrt(1 − 4x^{2})).]

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

If [MATH: y = \arcoth{e^x},] then [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}y}{ extrm{d}x}=]

[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}}{ extrm{d}x}(\arcoth x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2}.]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(arcoth e^{x}); = (1)/(1 − (e^{x})^{2}) ⋅ (e^{x})^{′}; = (1)/(1 − e^{2x}) ⋅ e^{x}; = (e^{x})/(1 − e^{2x}).]

items.title: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product and Quotient Rules

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

If [MATH: f(x) = \sin{x} \cdot \arcsch{x},] then [MATH: f'(x) = \cos{x} \arcsch{x} + g(x).] What is [MATH: g(x)?]

[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

In this case, the expression for [MATH: f(x)] is a product [MATH: u(x) \cdot v(x)] with [MATH: u(x) = \sin{x}] and [MATH: v(x) = \arcsch{x}.]

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows: [MATH: f^{′}(x)|= u^{′}(x) ⋅ v(x) + u(x) ⋅ v^{′}(x); = (\sin x)^{′} ⋅ arcsch x + \sin x ⋅ (arcsch x)^{′}; = \cos x ⋅ arcsch x + \sin x ⋅ (− (1)/(|x|sqrt(1 + x^{2}))); = \cos xarcsch x + (− (\sin x)/(|x|sqrt(1 + x^{2})))_(⏟)_(g(x))]

Therefore, [MATH: g(x) = -\dfrac{\sin{x}}{|x|\sqrt{1+x^2}}.]
